verdict.tagline: Survival on a hostile island brings tense combat and creative building.
for_you_if: you can handle clunky combat mechanics
you want a tense wilderness experience
not_for_you_if: you need reliable base building structures
you require cross-play support with friends

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the building system as frustrating, restrictive, and difficult to use effectively when constructing custom structures or doors.

citations.review_text:
Bordering on unplayable. Super bummed.

I fell in love with Sons Of The Forest and so I decided to try the first game as well. 
The building system is horrible. I cannot build a functional door on my custom building for the life of me. When I finish building the walls it sometimes shows a second blueprint on top of the first one so it's basically prompting me to double build a structure. What that is about, I have no idea. You also can't remove building blocks you've already placed, you gotta ♥♥♥♥ the whole thing up with an axe to destroy it. And when a building eventually collapses on you because ♥♥♥♥ you, you get like 1 log back from the 90 you used to build said structure.

You play as Timmy's dad, who's probably dying of COPD judging by the sounds he makes after running a few steps. The survival part is pretty merciless even on normal which could be forgivable if the building system wasn't so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. Like you can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ catch a break in this game. The story? Hell if I know, all the game threw at me was that I'm Timmy's dad and I assume I have to look for my son. That's it. 

Let's look at the bright side though, the developers have corrected most of their mistakes and made an absolutely fantastic, stylish, super fun sequel to this odd, clunky wheezing simulator.

I really wanted to enjoy The Forest, but it turned out to be a big letdown. It quickly becomes a repetitive lumberjack simulator filled with endless tree chopping and resource grinding.

The world feels empty, building is frustratingly restrictive, caves are way too dark, and the cannibals become annoying rather than scary. Hunger management is also too punishing early on.

Great idea, poor execution. Disappointed.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe combat as janky or finicky with poor hit detection.

citations.review_text:
[b]The Forest[/b]

Decent survival horror game. I didn't have the patience to get really get into it but there's some deep story and a good amount of variety in the survival mechanics. The game gives you a lot of different stuff you can find and stuff you can build while still retaining a good degree of realism. Combat can be kind of finicky but enemies are pretty terrifying and formidable.

[b]Rating: 5.0/10[/b]

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/_esquie_/]—Esquie[/url]

A survival crafting game with almost no reason to actually engage in the base-building mechanics. Combat is easy but exceptionally janky (poor hit detection). The story is somewhat interesting but very poorly told. 

This game does not hold up in 2026. There are numerous other games in this genre that do everything better.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that base building is hindered by structures being easily destroyed by enemies and buildings disintegrating rather than dropping materials.

citations.review_text:
The Forest as a game is a mystery to me - because I simply can not understand how an unfinished unoriginal game that has nothing impressive in it can go out of early access and still get this much praise.
[list]
    [*] I will start with the most obvious problem: basebuilding. While the game advertises itself with “build a base at day, defend it at night”, the base in question is broken on each and every level. First, building it takes a ridiculous amount of time because of the volume of the required resources. To make things worse - cutting all those trees to make a base makes the local population more aggressive and attacks on your base more often and as a result - instead of being more safe you end up being less safe with a base. The next reason why your base sucks that much is the fact that all of the things you build can be destroyed just in a couple of hits by some monsters or in under a minute by a group of cannibals - and destroyed buildings don’t just drop their materials - they disintegrate forcing you to waste even more time on logging and building. And the last problem with the base makes the whole situation just ridiculous - you don’t even need a base, as enemies are incapable of following you into caves or onto the boat where you can sleep freely and securely.
    [*] Survival elements. I will never stop hating survival systems where the food and water are abundant and extremely easy to get, but the bars run out so fast that you are constantly nagged with hunger and thirst. And just so you understand how easy the food situation is here - you can forage for berries, hunt for wildlife or eat your enemies - and each of those options can sustain you easily, not to mention that you can combine them however you like.
    [*] Combat. Oh god, I haven’t seen that much jank in a while. Sure, on one hand locals behave in an interesting way, with their running, screaming from a distance and everything, but when it comes to a fight having those lunatics run in and …

I enjoyed the first few hours but then I quickly came to find the gameplay loop a little too annoying to enjoy myself any longer. I don't really understand how this has such good reviews. There were some things i like and disliked about this. 

The Bad:
- The food and energy run out way too quickly and yet despite this there is an overabundance of food and water that is constantly respawning. It just turns it into an annoying tedious thing I have to constantly deal with. 
- Most of my time was spent walking around in caves which are scarry because they are filled with cannibals and eldritch horror monsters but I just can't see a thing while I'm fighting them, so again it is annoying. 
- There isn't really a reason to build bases other than to satisfy your creativity. The enemies just easily destroy your buildings like its nothing and you can actually accidentally hit your own building very easily if you are fighting cannibals near it. 
- I didn't finish the story but what i did play felt unintuitive to progress and not particularly interesting.
- The combat is terrible. it is very difficult to hit enemies with your weapons and basic enemies take something like 20 spear stabs to kill. Despite this, the enemies are laughably easy to kill because you just side strafe all their attacks. 
- you are constantly bombarded by patrols of cannibals so you never get time to rest, explore, and build. 
- Exploration wasn't very rewarding, I swam out to an interesting looking island only be rewarded with absolutely nothing being there.

The Good:
- The crafting system is interesting because there are no crafting recipes, just you jamming a bunch of stuff together until you find out what combines into what. 
- The game definitely has some scary moments.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players note missing cross-play support and building alignment issues alongside unique inventory mechanics.

claims.claim: The inventory system displays collected items spread out on a tarp on the floor rather than using a traditional grid layout.

citations.review_text:
The game has a very unique way to introduce the mysterious lore behind it: You're left completely alone, on an unknown island, with some really messed up wildlife ( Cannibals and mutants ). Your main objective, finding your son, becomes a whole lot more than you expected. Such a simple task turns into an unimaginable nightmare. The loneliness subconsciously pushes you to explore the terrain; you find wrecks, underwater caves, villages, weirds emblems - all sorts of unknown structures. 
As many say: Don't jugde a book by it's cover. You start off with an ordinary plane crash, and really, and I mean really soon, you realise that you are not only playing a survival game, you're playing a story-deep horror game. There is much more to explore than you think.
This game has an amazing way to picture an inventory, unlike most survival game, The Forest does not have a grid, with HUD styles - it has an original way to shows collected items: On the floor, protected by a tarp. How they managed to make an inventory feel like an inventory will forever surprise me.
The creepy, and hostile inhabitants of the island makes the game somewhat challenging. The final boss actually feels like a boss rather than a simple enemy. Overall, the PvE is highly focused, and combat is near unskippable.
Multiplayer is really fun, and can sometimes be hillarious; the bigest downside is that cross-playing is disabled... Meaning that a playstation player will never be able to have an adventure with a pc user. In my opinion, adding this would easily boost the game from a 4.2/5, to a solid 4.8/5.
Overall, harsh survival and interessting story which follows in the 2nd game: Sons of The Forest. And funny multiplayer, I give this game an excellent 4.2/5.
i am shocked by how this game is open world and you can do what you want! i also love the inventory system too!

Played for 10 years with various friend groups. The goofy antics you can get up to while building a base, scavenging for supplies, and fighting the nightmares of the island make for great replayability. I do wish there was a better system for making a map available, but they fixed that issue in Sons of the Forest, so it's aight.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the building system as frustrating due to components failing to line up properly and directional limitations on doors and ropes.

citations.review_text: I've played this about 100 hours now and I wish I hadn't bought it. It's buggy and incomplete and at this point, it doesn't appear the makers have any intention of coming back to fix it. Building *should* be amazing in this game, but it's nothing but a series of disappointments and frustration where you have to keep going back and tearing down work you've put a lot of time into because *one thing* doesn't work right.  Things don't line up properly, you can open a door from one side but not the other, you can climb down a rope but not up again...it's just an exercise in frustration every time I forget how frustrating it is, see some gameplay on Youtube and open it up to give it another try.
